日.meaningMnemonic: The sun rises in the morning and sets at night. Everything that happens while the sun is up fills one whole day.
日.readingMnemonic: Each day you find a sunny niche by the window to sit in. Niche sounds like にち, the reading of day. It can also be read じつ in some words.

一.meaningMnemonic: There is only one plank across the stream, so only one person can cross at a time. One plank means one.
一.readingMnemonic: Standing on that one plank, you get an itch on your back and cannot reach it without falling. Itch sounds like いち.

国.meaningMnemonic: A monarch stands inside a corral with a speck of gold on the crown. Everything inside that fence belongs to the monarch, and that land is a country.
国.readingMnemonic: The whole country has one royal cook who feeds every citizen. Cook sounds like こく.

人.meaningMnemonic: The walker is always on the move. Every walker you pass on the street is a person.
人.readingMnemonic: That person is carrying a bottle of gin home after a long day. Gin sounds like じん. In some words it is read にん instead.

年.meaningMnemonic: With a swoosh, a beggar pulls a plank off the drying rack and carves one notch in it. He adds a notch every time winter comes around, counting each year.
年.readingMnemonic: A kind nun gives the beggar a warm meal once a year. Nun sounds like ねん.

大.meaningMnemonic: This starfish stretches its arms as wide as it can to look impressive. It wants you to see how large it is.
大.readingMnemonic: The large starfish took a bath in purple dye and now it glows. Dye sounds like だい. It can also be read たい.

十.meaningMnemonic: Write a plus sign and count its four arms, then count the ends and the middle twice for good luck. Somehow you always end up at ten.
十.readingMnemonic: You win ten shiny prizes, and every one is a jewel. Jewel sounds like じゅう.

二.meaningMnemonic: Bunk beds hold exactly two sleepers, one on top and one below. Bunk beds mean two.
二.readingMnemonic: Climbing to the top of the bunk beds, you bang your knee on the rail. Knee sounds like に.

本.meaningMnemonic: Shout timber, and the tree falls onto a plank laid on the ground. The wood is pressed into paper and bound into a book.
本.readingMnemonic: A goose sees you reading that book and gives a loud honk. Honk sounds like ほん.

中.meaningMnemonic: A pole is pushed straight through the middle of a hatch. The pole is now in the hatch, right inside it.
中.readingMnemonic: Stuck in the middle of the hatch, you chew on a sandwich while you wait. Chew sounds like ちゅう.

長.meaningMnemonic: Her long hair has not been cut in years and now reaches the floor. That hair is long.
長.readingMnemonic: She has to tie up all that long hair before she sits down to chow. Chow sounds like ちょう.

出.meaningMnemonic: A pole stands in a bucket at the foot of three peaks. Climb the pole, step over the peaks, and you exit the valley.
出.readingMnemonic: On your way to the exit, green shoots spring up wherever you step. Shoots sounds like しゅつ.

三.meaningMnemonic: Put a plank under the bunk beds and you have three flat lines stacked up. Plank plus bunk beds makes three.
三.readingMnemonic: Three buckets of sand are piled on top of each other. Sand sounds like さん.

時.meaningMnemonic: You push a stick an inch into the soil and watch its shadow move with the sun. The shadow tells you the time.
時.readingMnemonic: It is time to leave, so you jump into your jeep. Jeep sounds like じ.

行.meaningMnemonic: At the crossroads you can turn down any side street you like. Whichever way you choose, you keep going.
行.readingMnemonic: Before going out, you grab your coat from the hook. Coat sounds like こう. It is also read ぎょう in some words.

見.meaningMnemonic: The watcher has one giant eyeball and walks around on stilts to get a better view. All it does is see.
見.readingMnemonic: The watcher sees a dog sleeping in its kennel. Kennel sounds like けん.

月.meaningMnemonic: A thin crescent hangs in the sky and slowly grows full, then shrinks again. That cycle takes one month.
月.readingMnemonic: Once a month you try to get a good photo of the crescent. Get sounds like げつ. It is also read がつ for the months of the year.

後.meaningMnemonic: Down a side street, someone walks on dragging feet, trailing a tiny thread from their coat. They are always lagging behind.
後.readingMnemonic: A goat trots behind them, nibbling the thread. Goat sounds like ご. It is also read こう in some words.

前.meaningMnemonic: A deer with antlers stands on a plank, holding a sickle under the crescent. It wants to go first and steps in front.
前.readingMnemonic: The deer calmly meditates before stepping in front, completely zen. Zen sounds like ぜん.

生.meaningMnemonic: A seedling pushes up through the ground and opens its first leaves. It is the start of a new life.
生.readingMnemonic: Every new life deserves a chance to say hello. Say sounds like せい. It is also read しょう in some words.

五.meaningMnemonic: A high five uses your whole hand. Count the fingers on that hand and you get five.
五.readingMnemonic: Five goats line up to give you a high five with their hooves. Goat sounds like ご.

間.meaningMnemonic: The sun peeks through the gap between the saloon doors. That gap is an interval, the space between two things.
間.readingMnemonic: Someone has wedged a can in the space between the doors to keep them open. Can sounds like かん.

上.meaningMnemonic: A fortune stick stands upright on a plank, pointing to the sky. It always points above.
上.readingMnemonic: A joker climbs up above everyone and juggles on the plank. Joker sounds like じょう.

東.meaningMnemonic: A pole of timber stands in the middle of the paddy, laid across with a plank. The sun rises right behind it every morning, because it faces east.
東.readingMnemonic: Facing east at dawn, you dip one toe into the cold paddy. Toe sounds like とう.

四.meaningMnemonic: Someone on stilts is trapped in a corral and pokes a stilt out of each corner. That makes four.
四.readingMnemonic: Four sheep wander into the corral to keep them company. Sheep sounds like し. It is also read よん and よ.

下.meaningMnemonic: A plank lies flat with a pole hanging down from it, and a fortune stick dangles off the end of the pole. Everything here points down, below the plank.
下.readingMnemonic: You park your car below the bridge to keep it out of the rain. Car sounds like か. It is also read げ, and した on its own.

山.meaningMnemonic: Three peaks rise from one wide base against the sky. Put them together and you have a mountain.
山.readingMnemonic: At the foot of the mountain the ground turns to soft sand. Sand sounds like さん. It is also read せん, and やま on its own.

午.meaningMnemonic: With a swoosh, a beggar hangs his only shirt on a drying rack shaped like a plus sign. He waits for the sun to climb to the top of the sky, because by noon it will be dry.
午.readingMnemonic: At noon every day a goat wanders over to nibble the shirt. Goat sounds like ご.

先.meaningMnemonic: With a swoosh, someone leaps off the soil onto a pair of stilts and strides away. Up there they are always ahead, there before everyone else.
先.readingMnemonic: Being ahead, they spot a lucky cent on the path before anyone. Cent sounds like せん. On its own it is read さき.

今.meaningMnemonic: Rain starts pouring, so you snap open your umbrella over a plank bench and sit right there. You need shelter now, not later.
今.readingMnemonic: Under the umbrella you eat an ice cream cone right now, before it melts. Cone sounds like こん. On its own it is read いま.

金.meaningMnemonic: Under an umbrella, a monarch with a huge mustache and a crown of antlers counts a pile of ingots. Every single one is made of gold.
金.readingMnemonic: Only the king may touch that gold. King sounds like きん. It is also read かね when it means money.

九.meaningMnemonic: Your bent elbow sticks out just like the curl of the number nine. Before every game you bend it nine times, never more than nine.
九.readingMnemonic: Then you pick up your pool cue and line up the shot. Cue sounds like きゅう. It is also read く in some words.

入.meaningMnemonic: The tunnel has a low, pointed opening. Duck your head and enter.
入.readingMnemonic: Inside the tunnel, a little newt scurries in ahead of you. Newt sounds like にゅう. As a verb it is read はい or い.

学.meaningMnemonic: A toddler hides under a blanket with a book, thinking so hard that steam rises from its head. Even this little one loves to study.
学.readingMnemonic: Grown ups gawk at the toddler who studies all night. Gawk sounds like がく. As a verb it is read まな.

高.meaningMnemonic: A thumbtack holds a flag on the roof of a tower. Climb up through a hatch, past a goalpost on the balcony, and you see just how tall it is.
高.readingMnemonic: It is so tall and windy at the top that you need a coat. Coat sounds like こう. On its own it is read たか.

円.meaningMnemonic: A ball sails through the goalpost, bounces off a pole, and spins around a plank pinned down with a thumbtack. It keeps rolling in a perfect circle.
円.readingMnemonic: It rolls round and round with no end. End sounds like えん. The same word is the yen, the money of Japan.

子.meaningMnemonic: A toddler waves its arms and wobbles across the room. Every toddler is a child.
子.readingMnemonic: At bedtime the child counts sheep to fall asleep. Sheep sounds like し. On its own it is read こ.

外.meaningMnemonic: At dusk you take your fortune stick and go read it under the open sky. You cannot read a fortune indoors; you have to be outside.
外.readingMnemonic: Outside, a guy is already waiting with his own fortune stick. Guy sounds like がい. On its own it is read そと.

八.meaningMnemonic: This mustache has four curls on each side. Count them all and you get eight.
八.readingMnemonic: Trimming all those curls takes a tiny hatchet and a steady hand. Hatchet sounds like はち. It is also read や in some words.

六.meaningMnemonic: A thumbtack pins a fake mustache to the wall. It has exactly six hairs, so this one means six.
六.readingMnemonic: Six rocks hold the mustache down when the wind blows. Rock sounds like ろく. It is also read む in some words.

来.meaningMnemonic: You fix a pole between the bunk beds with a thumbtack, light a sparkler, and stand it on a log of timber. It is the signal for your friends to come over.
来.readingMnemonic: They come carrying loaves of rye bread. Rye sounds like らい. As a verb it is read く, as in くる.

気.meaningMnemonic: A beggar lets out a long breath on a cold day. A speck of light swirls through it with a swoosh, and you can feel his spirit.
気.readingMnemonic: That spirit is the key to his good mood. Key sounds like き. It is also read け in some words.

小.meaningMnemonic: One drop falls and makes a splash, with two droplets jumping out to the sides. It is only a little splash.
小.readingMnemonic: The little splash puts on a show for the ants nearby. Show sounds like しょう. On its own it is read ちい, as in ちいさい.

七.meaningMnemonic: A swan grips a ladle in its beak and stirs the pond with a swoosh. It always stops after exactly seven stirs.
七.readingMnemonic: Then it dries the ladle on seven clean sheets. Sheet sounds like しち. It is also read なな.

話.meaningMnemonic: Someone pops out of a hatch with a lollipop in one hand and a megaphone in the other. They will not stop telling you a long tale.
話.readingMnemonic: The tale is all about a giant waffle. Waffle sounds like わ. As a verb it is read はな, as in はなす.

女.meaningMnemonic: The dancer spins across the stage in a long gown. She is a woman who owns the spotlight.
女.readingMnemonic: Every morning the woman goes for a jog before practice. Jog sounds like じょ. On its own it is read おんな.

北.meaningMnemonic: Climb the ladder with a ladle in your hand and point it at the stars. The handle points to the North Star, so you know which way is north.
北.readingMnemonic: Up north, everyone plays ice hockey. Hockey sounds like ほく. On its own it is read きた.

百.meaningMnemonic: Line up milk cartons along a long plank. Keep going until the plank holds one hundred of them.
百.readingMnemonic: A thirsty yak drinks all one hundred cartons. Yak sounds like ひゃく.

書.meaningMnemonic: You sit in the sun with a quill and a blank page. Dip the quill in ink and start to write.
書.readingMnemonic: You write a story about the sea shore. Shore sounds like しょ. As a verb it is read か, as in かく.

名.meaningMnemonic: At dusk it is too dark to see faces, so you open a hatch and call out. Everyone answers with their name.
名.readingMnemonic: A lion shakes its mane when it hears its name. Mane sounds like めい. On its own it is read な.

千.meaningMnemonic: With a swoosh of the pen, you draw a plus sign, then another, and another. You keep going until you have drawn a thousand.
千.readingMnemonic: Each one earns you a cent, so a thousand of them make ten dollars. Cent sounds like せん. It is also read ち in some words.

半.meaningMnemonic: A deer with antlers stands between the bunk beds, and a pole runs down the middle like a giant plus sign. It splits the room exactly in half.
半.readingMnemonic: Give me your hand and I will give you half my snack. Hand sounds like はん.

語.meaningMnemonic: Someone climbs out of a hatch, gives you a high five, and shouts into a megaphone. Every word comes out loud and clear.
語.readingMnemonic: Even the goat learns a few words. Goat sounds like ご. As a verb it is read かた, as in かたる.

土.meaningMnemonic: Kneel in the garden and pat the soil flat with both hands. This kanji is simply soil, the earth that everything grows in.
土.readingMnemonic: Mix the soil with water and it turns into a lump of dough. Dough sounds like ど. On its own it is read つち.

木.meaningMnemonic: Long before anyone shouts timber, the trunk stands tall with branches above and roots below. It is a living tree.
木.readingMnemonic: You pick a bouquet of blossoms from the tree. Bouquet sounds like ぼく. It is also read もく, and き on its own.

南.meaningMnemonic: A deer with antlers sets up a drying rack under a goalpost and paints a plus sign on top. The laundry dries fast because it faces the warm sun, which means it faces south.
南.readingMnemonic: In the south they bake warm naan in clay ovens. Naan sounds like なん. On its own it is read みなみ.

万.meaningMnemonic: With a swoosh, a pole spins across a plank, again and again. It spins ten thousand times before it stops.
万.readingMnemonic: One patient man counts every spin. Man sounds like まん. It is also read ばん in some words.

白.meaningMnemonic: Tip the milk carton and pour. What comes out is white.
白.readingMnemonic: A hawk swoops down to sip the white milk. Hawk sounds like はく. On its own it is read しろ.

天.meaningMnemonic: A starfish climbs to the top of the bunk beds, then onto a plank laid across them, reaching up and up. It is trying to touch the heavens.
天.readingMnemonic: It pitches a tent up in the heavens. Tent sounds like てん. It is also read あま in some words.

右.meaningMnemonic: With a swoosh, a plank slides across a hatch. You always push it shut with your right hand.
右.readingMnemonic: Green ooze leaks out of the right side of the hatch. Ooze sounds like う. It is also read ゆう, and みぎ on its own.

川.meaningMnemonic: Each line here is a little creek trickling down the hill. Three creeks running side by side join up into one strong stream.
川.readingMnemonic: Toss a cent into the stream and make a wish. Cent sounds like せん. On its own it is read かわ.

水.meaningMnemonic: The fountain in the town square sprays out in every direction. What pours out of every fountain is water.
水.readingMnemonic: The fountain water tastes surprisingly sweet. Sweet sounds like すい. On its own it is read みず.

男.meaningMnemonic: A farmer puts every muscle into plowing the rice paddy. In the old picture, this strong worker in the field stands for a man, a male.
男.readingMnemonic: When the plowing is done, he does a little victory dance. Dance sounds like だん. It is also read なん, and おとこ on its own.

西.meaningMnemonic: Every evening you leave the cookie jar on the windowsill where the sun goes down. The jar always faces the setting sun, toward the west.
西.readingMnemonic: Say goodbye to the sun as it sinks in the west. Say sounds like せい. It is also read さい, and にし on its own.

電.meaningMnemonic: A drizzle falls over the rice paddy, and a swan stretches its neck up into the storm. Lightning strikes, and the whole paddy crackles with electricity.
電.readingMnemonic: You hide in your den until the power comes back on. Den sounds like でん.

校.meaningMnemonic: With scissors you trim a block of timber into a desk and pin a notice to it with a thumbtack. You are at school, and the notice says it is time for your exam.
校.readingMnemonic: You left your coat at school on the day of the exam. Coat sounds like こう. It is also read きょう in some words.

聞.meaningMnemonic: You press your earlobe right up against the saloon doors. You cannot see inside, but you can hear.
聞.readingMnemonic: Through the doors you hear someone order a sticky bun. Bun sounds like ぶん. It is also read もん, and き as a verb, as in きく.

食.meaningMnemonic: You open your lunchbox at noon and find it packed to the lid. There is only one thing to do with it: eat.
食.readingMnemonic: You get a shock when a frog jumps out of your lunchbox. Shock sounds like しょく. As a verb it is read た, as in たべる, or く, as in くう.

車.meaningMnemonic: Bolt an engine onto the wagon and it no longer needs a horse to pull it. Now it is a car.
車.readingMnemonic: A shark sits behind the wheel, honking at everyone. Shark sounds like しゃ. On its own it is read くるま.

何.meaningMnemonic: Your sidekick lies on a plank, dangling a fishhook through a hatch in the floor. Something big tugs on the line, and you both gasp: what?
何.readingMnemonic: Whatever it is, it pulls so hard that a whole car comes up through the hatch. Car sounds like か. On its own it is read なに, or なん before some sounds.

毎.meaningMnemonic: A beggar builds a barricade around a bird nest to guard the eggs. He checks on it again and again, every single day.
毎.readingMnemonic: He has to, because hungry mice keep sneaking past the barricade. Mice sounds like まい.

母.meaningMnemonic: Behind the barricade sits a bird nest, and one bird never leaves it. She keeps the eggs warm because she is their mother.
母.readingMnemonic: When the eggs hatch, the mother takes her chicks out on a boat. Boat sounds like ぼ. On its own it is read はは.

火.meaningMnemonic: Sparks leap up from the campfire into the night sky. Every campfire starts with one thing: fire.
火.readingMnemonic: Never park your car too close to the fire. Car sounds like か. On its own it is read ひ.

読.meaningMnemonic: A knight wobbles up on stilts with a blanket over his shoulders and a megaphone in his hand. He unrolls a long scroll and begins to read.
読.readingMnemonic: He reads the news aloud to every ship down at the dock. Dock sounds like どく. As a verb it is read よ, as in よむ.

友.meaningMnemonic: With a swoosh, you throw a plank across the stream and walk over it side by side, crossed fingers held up for luck. The one who crosses with you is your friend.
友.readingMnemonic: Your friend is a unicorn who always lets you ride on its back. Unicorn sounds like ゆう. On its own it is read とも.

休.meaningMnemonic: Your sidekick leans against a big timber and closes their eyes. After all that work, it is time to rest.
休.readingMnemonic: Your coach gives you the cue to sit down and rest. Cue sounds like きゅう.

父.meaningMnemonic: Only one person in the house is allowed to hold the big scissors. Every birthday he cuts the cake into perfectly fair slices, because that is what a father does.
父.readingMnemonic: Father cooks a pot of food for the whole family every Sunday. Food sounds like ふ.

雨.meaningMnemonic: A light drizzle starts to fall from the gray sky. It grows heavier and heavier until you are soaked in real rain.
雨.readingMnemonic: Rain soaks the ground until mud starts to ooze between your toes. Ooze sounds like う.

同.meaningMnemonic: A goalpost stands around a hatch with a plank across it. Every goalpost on the field looks exactly the same.
同.readingMnemonic: Two deer in the forest look the same, so you cannot tell which doe is which. Doe sounds like どう.

力.meaningMnemonic: Muscle on its own means power. Flex a muscle and you feel its strength.
力.readingMnemonic: A rook in a chess game has the power to sweep across the whole board. Rook sounds like りょく.

問.meaningMnemonic: A hatch sits behind saloon doors. Every cowboy who walks in stops to ask a question about what is behind it.
問.readingMnemonic: A curious monk keeps asking the same question all day. Monk sounds like もん.

明.meaningMnemonic: The sun and the crescent shine side by side, so the sky is never dark. Everything looks bright.
明.readingMnemonic: A horse shakes its mane in the bright sunlight. Mane sounds like めい.

京.meaningMnemonic: Above a hatch, a thumbtack pins a big map to the wall. A splash of red paint marks the most important city on it: the capital.
京.readingMnemonic: Every corner of the capital has a kiosk selling newspapers. Kiosk sounds like きょう.

目.meaningMnemonic: A huge eyeball rolls into view and stops. It blinks once and stares right back at you with one big eye.
目.readingMnemonic: Your friend makes a face, and you mock them by staring with one wide eye. Mock sounds like もく.

言.meaningMnemonic: The megaphone on its own means to say. Lift it to your mouth and say a word.
言.readingMnemonic: A gent in a top hat stands up to say a few words. Gent sounds like げん.

体.meaningMnemonic: Your sidekick props a plank against a timber to train every muscle. After that workout your whole body aches.
体.readingMnemonic: You tie a ribbon around your body for the race. Tie sounds like たい.

田.meaningMnemonic: From above, the paddy is a square cut into four parts. Each part is flooded and green, a perfect rice field.
田.readingMnemonic: A bear has a den right next to the rice field. Den sounds like でん.

主.meaningMnemonic: A monarch stands tall with one speck of gold on top of the head. That speck shows who is in charge: the lord.
主.readingMnemonic: The lord wears one golden shoe so everyone knows who is in charge. Shoe sounds like しゅ.

不.meaningMnemonic: A pole, a swoosh, a plank, and a speck are thrown together in a mess that just does not work. It is all negative.
不.readingMnemonic: A sign at the buffet says no food allowed, the most negative rule you have ever seen. Food sounds like ふ.

作.meaningMnemonic: A beggar asks your sidekick for a place to sleep. The sidekick grabs a pole, a plank, and with a swoosh of rope ties them together. In minutes they make a small hut.
作.readingMnemonic: You make a sack out of old cloth to carry your tools. Sack sounds like さく.

以.meaningMnemonic: A walker uses a pole and a speck of light to find the way. By means of those two things, the walker gets home.
以.readingMnemonic: An eel slips through the water by means of its long tail. Eel sounds like い.

多.meaningMnemonic: Dusk falls, then dusk falls again, one evening after another. The days pile up until there are many.
多.readingMnemonic: You spread black tar on so many roads that you lose count. Tar sounds like た.

界.meaningMnemonic: Stilts walk across a paddy holding an umbrella. Wherever they wander, the whole world opens up before them.
界.readingMnemonic: You fly a kite so high it can see the whole world. Kite sounds like かい.

画.meaningMnemonic: A plank lies across a paddy that sits in a bucket. Together they look like one brush stroke in a picture.
画.readingMnemonic: An artist paints a picture of a glowing gas lamp. Gas sounds like が.

売.meaningMnemonic: A knight on stilts wraps his things in a blanket. He stands tall above the crowd and shouts so he can sell them.
売.readingMnemonic: Once the knight sells everything, they wave bye to the crowd. Bye sounds like ばい.

使.meaningMnemonic: Your sidekick takes a swoosh of rope and a plank and climbs through a hatch. The sidekick knows how to use every tool.
使.readingMnemonic: You use a sheep dog to round up the sheep. Sheep sounds like し.

計.meaningMnemonic: A megaphone sits next to a plus sign. Someone shouts numbers through it to measure and plan a big party.
計.readingMnemonic: The party plan includes measuring flour for a huge cake. Cake sounds like けい.

朝.meaningMnemonic: The sun comes up between two plus signs while the crescent is still fading. It is morning.
朝.readingMnemonic: Every morning you chow down on a big breakfast. Chow sounds like ちょう.

公.meaningMnemonic: A mustache sits over an arrowhead on a statue in the town square. That statue belongs to the public.
公.readingMnemonic: The public statue wears a coat in winter. Coat sounds like こう.

持.meaningMnemonic: You use a grabber to scoop up some soil. You measure out exactly one inch of it and keep it to hold.
持.readingMnemonic: You hold the soil in a jeep. Jeep sounds like じ.

野.meaningMnemonic: A halberd and a fishhook lie forgotten on an old farmstead. All around them, flat empty land stretches out for miles: the plains.
野.readingMnemonic: A yacht sails across the plains as if it were the sea. Yacht sounds like や.

思.meaningMnemonic: You stand at the edge of a paddy while your pulse slows down. In the quiet, you finally have time to think.
思.readingMnemonic: You think about sheep in the paddy. Sheep sounds like し.

家.meaningMnemonic: A hog lives in the attic. That attic is part of your house.
家.readingMnemonic: You park the car in front of the house. Car sounds like か.

世.meaningMnemonic: A pole and a plank prop up a trellis. Vines grow on it for a whole generation.
世.readingMnemonic: Each generation has a lot to say. Say sounds like せい.

正.meaningMnemonic: You lay a plank across the top of a stop sign. It sits perfectly level, so the sign is now correct.
正.readingMnemonic: You say the correct answer. Say sounds like せい.

安.meaningMnemonic: After a long show, a dancer climbs up to the attic. She lies on a soft rug and stretches out to relax.
安.readingMnemonic: An ant relaxes next to the dancer. Ant sounds like あん.

院.meaningMnemonic: A staircase leads up to an attic over bunk beds on stilts. Kickoff for the big institution happens there.
院.readingMnemonic: The institution started as a small inn. Inn sounds like いん.

心.meaningMnemonic: Put your hand on your chest and feel your pulse. Each beat comes from your heart.
心.readingMnemonic: You hold your heart and your shin aches with love. Shin sounds like しん.

教.meaningMnemonic: A toddler with a walking cane and a baton gets taught by a beggar. Even a beggar can teach.
教.readingMnemonic: The lesson happens at a kiosk. Kiosk sounds like きょう.

文.meaningMnemonic: A brush moves slowly across the page in careful calligraphy. Stroke by stroke, the words join up into a sentence.
文.readingMnemonic: You write a sentence on a bun. Bun sounds like ぶん.

元.meaningMnemonic: Bunk beds on stilts mark the kickoff. That is the beginning of everything.
元.readingMnemonic: A gent stands at the beginning of the line. Gent sounds like げん.

重.meaningMnemonic: A pole, a swoosh, a plank, and the sun sit on a farmstead. Carrying all of that is heavy.
重.readingMnemonic: A heavy jewel sits on top. Jewel sounds like じゅう.

近.meaningMnemonic: Someone sets a woodcutter axe on a conveyor belt. It rolls closer and closer until it is right next to you, far too near.
近.readingMnemonic: The king stands near you. King sounds like きん.

考.meaningMnemonic: An old man leans on his walking cane and pulls up his hood. He stays still for a long time, needing to consider the question.

知.meaningMnemonic: A beggar throws a dart at a hatch and hits it. The beggar knows the trick.
知.readingMnemonic: A cheetah knows the fastest way. Cheetah sounds like ち.

道.meaningMnemonic: A conveyor belt carries a self portrait wearing antlers and a scarf. It rolls on and on, showing you the road and the way.

別.meaningMnemonic: A sickle cuts a hatch, a muscle tears a hood. Everything gets split into separate pieces.

物.meaningMnemonic: A banner, an ox, a hood, and a swoosh lie in the barn. Each one is a thing.

品.meaningMnemonic: A hatch opens on top of a tall crate stack. Inside every box are things to sell: goods.
品.readingMnemonic: A hinge holds each crate of goods shut. Hinge sounds like ひん.

死.meaningMnemonic: A plank, a ladle, and bones lie out at dusk. Something met its death here.
死.readingMnemonic: Sheep stand around the bones in silence. Sheep sounds like し.

特.meaningMnemonic: An ox stands on an inch of soil wearing a crown. That ox is special.
特.readingMnemonic: A toucan lands on the special ox. Toucan sounds like とく.

私.meaningMnemonic: A wheat stalk grows next to an arrowhead in your private garden. It is all mine.
私.readingMnemonic: Your private garden is full of sheep. Sheep sounds like し.

始.meaningMnemonic: A dancer opens a hatch and fires an arrowhead into the air. The show can now begin.
始.readingMnemonic: The show begins with sheep on stage. Sheep sounds like し.

左.meaningMnemonic: A swoosh of wind knocks a plank off the girder. No matter how hard it blows, the plank always lands on the same side of you: the left.
左.readingMnemonic: You hold the saw in your left hand. Saw sounds like さ.

会.meaningMnemonic: Everyone climbs down from their bunk beds and grabs an umbrella. They follow an arrowhead sign down the hall to the big meeting.
会.readingMnemonic: At the meeting everyone flies a kite in the park. Kite sounds like かい.

事.meaningMnemonic: A plank, a hatch, a fishhook, and a rake are piled in the shed. Sorting them out is a matter you keep putting off.
事.readingMnemonic: You park the jeep by the shed while you deal with the matter. Jeep sounds like じ.

自.meaningMnemonic: The self portrait shows one big eyeball staring back. It is a picture of oneself.
自.readingMnemonic: You paint yourself driving a jeep. Jeep sounds like じ.

社.meaningMnemonic: Somebody has piled soil around an altar in the middle of the office. Every morning the staff pray there for good sales, because this is how the company works.

発.meaningMnemonic: Footprints lead out from under bunk beds and run off on stilts. Someone made a quick departure.

者.meaningMnemonic: A person with a walking cane shuffles along in the sun. Someone is out for a walk.
者.readingMnemonic: That someone is a shark with a cane. Shark sounds like しゃ.

地.meaningMnemonic: A whip cracks down hard on the soil. When the dust settles, a long mark is left in the ground.
地.readingMnemonic: A cheetah races across the ground. Cheetah sounds like ち.

業.meaningMnemonic: A monarch with antlers rides a ram pulling a plow across timber, a pole, and a plank. Running all that is a big business.
業.readingMnemonic: The business sells nothing but gyoza. Gyoza sounds like ぎょう.

方.meaningMnemonic: You stand at a crossroads, unsure where to go. The signpost points one arm out, showing you the direction.
方.readingMnemonic: A farmer points a hoe in the right direction. Hoe sounds like ほう.

新.meaningMnemonic: A woodcutter axe chops timber, a chili pepper, and antlers, and a thumbtack pins them to a podium. It is a brand new art piece.
新.readingMnemonic: You bang your shin on the new piece. Shin sounds like しん.

場.meaningMnemonic: A banner flies over soil in the sun, with a plank to sit on. That is the place to be.
場.readingMnemonic: A joker juggles in the middle of the place. Joker sounds like じょう.

員.meaningMnemonic: A mustache, an eyeball, a hatch, and a clam all wear name tags. Each one is an employee.
員.readingMnemonic: Every employee lives at the same inn. Inn sounds like いん.

立.meaningMnemonic: The podium on its own means to stand up. Step onto it and stand tall.
立.readingMnemonic: You stand up in a field of tall ritzy reeds. Ritzy sounds like りつ.

開.meaningMnemonic: Saloon doors swing open. A swoosh of pliers pulls a plank off the bunk beds blocking the way.
開.readingMnemonic: You open the door and kites fly in. Kite sounds like かい.

手.meaningMnemonic: You hold up your palm with all five fingers spread wide. That open palm is your hand.
手.readingMnemonic: You put a shoe on your hand like a puppet. Shoe sounds like しゅ.

代.meaningMnemonic: Your sidekick pulls up a tent stake and puts a new one in its place. That stake is a substitute.

動.meaningMnemonic: A pole, a plank, and the sun sit on a farmstead. A muscle with a swoosh of effort makes them all move.
動.readingMnemonic: A doe moves quickly through the field. Doe sounds like どう.

通.meaningMnemonic: A pennant on a toolbox rides the conveyor belt through the city. Traffic carries it everywhere.

理.meaningMnemonic: A monarch moves onto a farmstead and starts making rules. Every rule comes with a reason, because this monarch runs everything by logic.
理.readingMnemonic: The monarch explains the logic while snorkeling on a reef. Reef sounds like り.

題.meaningMnemonic: A clam with an eyeball and a mustache sits in the sun on a bolt of cloth, reading a page. The page has a topic written on top.
題.readingMnemonic: The topic is printed in bright dye. Dye sounds like だい.

意.meaningMnemonic: A chime rings on a podium in the sun, and your pulse jumps. A new idea pops into your head.
意.readingMnemonic: An eel swims through your idea. Eel sounds like い.

用.meaningMnemonic: The toolbox on its own means to utilize. Open it and put the tools to use.
用.readingMnemonic: You utilize a yoyo as a tool. Yoyo sounds like よう.

度.meaningMnemonic: Under the carport, a plank sits in a bucket with crossed fingers on top. You check the thermometer degrees again and again.

強.meaningMnemonic: An archer shoots a beetle with an arrowhead. That beetle is strong enough to survive.

運.meaningMnemonic: A wagon under a blanket rides the conveyor belt. The belt will carry it all the way to town.
運.readingMnemonic: You cannot undo the luck that carries you. Undo sounds like うん.

台.meaningMnemonic: An arrowhead balances on top of a hatch. The hatch is its pedestal.
台.readingMnemonic: You dye the pedestal bright red. Dye sounds like だい.

広.meaningMnemonic: An arrowhead lies all alone under the carport. The carport is so roomy that a hundred more could fit, because it is very wide.
広.readingMnemonic: A coat that wide covers the whole carport. Coat sounds like こう.

住.meaningMnemonic: A speck sits over the monarch, and the sidekick stands beside. Together they dwell in one small palace.
住.readingMnemonic: Where you dwell, you hide a jewel. Jewel sounds like じゅう.

真.meaningMnemonic: A plus sign sits on an eyeball, a plank lies below, and a mustache hangs under it all. Strange, but every word of it is true.
真.readingMnemonic: A kick to the shin tells you what is true. Shin sounds like しん.

少.readingMnemonic: Only a few people came to the show. Show sounds like しょう.

町.meaningMnemonic: A plank bridge crosses the paddy, and an old fishhook hangs on a post beside it. That sign marks the edge of a small town.
町.readingMnemonic: The whole town comes out for chow. Chow sounds like ちょう.

工.meaningMnemonic: A builder sets one girder in place, perfectly straight. That single girder shows off years of skill and craft.
工.readingMnemonic: You craft yourself a coat out of steel. Coat sounds like こう.

急.meaningMnemonic: You grab the rake and pull up your hood, your pulse racing. You have to hurry.
急.readingMnemonic: Hurry, that is your cue. Cue sounds like きゅう.

止.meaningMnemonic: A red stop sign stands at the corner. Every car that reaches it has to stop.
止.readingMnemonic: Stop the sheep at the gate. Sheep sounds like し.

送.meaningMnemonic: Antlers sit on a starfish, with a plank and bunk beds below. You load them all on the conveyor belt and send them away.

転.meaningMnemonic: A wagon rolls over bunk beds and an arrowhead. Its wheels revolve and the whole load turns over.
転.readingMnemonic: The tent revolves in the wind. Tent sounds like てん.

着.meaningMnemonic: A ram with antlers and one swoosh of wool stares with a big eyeball at the monarch's robe. It wants to don the robe and wear it.
着.readingMnemonic: You don a new jacket and chuck the old one. Chuck sounds like ちゃく.

店.meaningMnemonic: Under the carport, a fortune stick pokes out of a hatch. It is a little store that sells fortunes.
店.readingMnemonic: The store is just a tent. Tent sounds like てん.

質.meaningMnemonic: Two woodcutter axes split a clam open. Under the eyeball and the mustache there is real substance, a pearl of quality.
質.readingMnemonic: A comedian's shtick needs substance. Shtick sounds like しつ.

待.meaningMnemonic: On a side street, you move the soil one inch at a time. You wait and wait.
待.readingMnemonic: You wait in a suit and tie. Tie sounds like たい.

試.meaningMnemonic: You shout through the megaphone and bang a stake into the girder. You test whether it holds.
試.readingMnemonic: You test the sheep. Sheep sounds like し.

族.meaningMnemonic: A beggar follows the signpost, dodging a dart. They find their tribe at last.
族.readingMnemonic: Every tribe has its own zodiac. Zodiac sounds like ぞく.

早.meaningMnemonic: The sun rises over a plus sign. You are up early.
早.readingMnemonic: You wash with soap early in the morning. Soap sounds like そう.

映.meaningMnemonic: The sun shines on a starfish under a blanket, and with a swoosh the light bounces back. The water reflects it.
映.readingMnemonic: An ace card reflects in the mirror. Ace sounds like えい.

親.meaningMnemonic: A thumbtack on a podium, antlers on a chili pepper, timber at the base, and a watcher beside it all. That watcher is a parent keeping an eye out.
親.readingMnemonic: A parent taps your shin. Shin sounds like しん.

仕.meaningMnemonic: The sidekick stands next to the knight. Their job is to attend to the knight.
仕.readingMnemonic: The sidekick attends to the sheep. Sheep sounds like し.

去.meaningMnemonic: An arrowhead sticks out of the soil. The archer is long gone.
去.readingMnemonic: The archer has gone to Kyoto. Kyoto sounds like きょ.

味.meaningMnemonic: Through the hatch you see a pole, bunk beds, timber, a thumbtack, and a mustache dipped in soup. Every one adds flavor.
味.readingMnemonic: The meat is full of flavor. Meat sounds like み.

写.meaningMnemonic: You hide under a blanket with your hood pulled up. By the light of a torch, you trace the plank's outline onto paper to copy it.
写.readingMnemonic: A shark copies every move you make. Shark sounds like しゃ.

字.meaningMnemonic: A toddler finds crayons in the attic. On every wall, the toddler scribbles letters, one character at a time.
字.readingMnemonic: The toddler writes letters in a jeep. Jeep sounds like じ.

夜.meaningMnemonic: Dusk fades, and your sidekick climbs up to pin a thumbtack in the sky like a star. The sky turns dark, and it is night.
夜.readingMnemonic: A yacht sails out at night. Yacht sounds like や.

音.meaningMnemonic: The chime rings above the podium as the sun rises. What a lovely sound.
音.readingMnemonic: Chop an onion and listen to the sound. Onion sounds like おん.

注.meaningMnemonic: The monarch holds a jug over a cup. Droplets fall out, speck by speck, as the monarch begins to pour.
注.readingMnemonic: Pour the soup, then chew. Chew sounds like ちゅう.

古.meaningMnemonic: A plus sign is carved over a hatch. The carving is very old.
古.readingMnemonic: The cocoa in the cupboard is old. Cocoa sounds like こ.

悪.meaningMnemonic: A pole drives through a hatch, a plank on top, and the pulse below starts to race. Something bad is coming.
悪.readingMnemonic: The acrobat had a bad fall. Acrobat sounds like あく.

週.meaningMnemonic: Soil and a hatch sit inside a goalpost on a conveyor belt. It takes a full week to come around.
週.readingMnemonic: You shuffle the cards once a week. Shuffle sounds like しゅう.

歩.meaningMnemonic: At the stop sign there is a big splash and a swoosh of water. You step over the puddle and keep going on your walk.
歩.readingMnemonic: A hobo walks the long road. Hobo sounds like ほ.

春.meaningMnemonic: A walker climbs the bunk beds and a starfish lies on a plank under the sun. It is springtime.
春.readingMnemonic: Nobody can shun springtime. Shun sounds like しゅん.

館.meaningMnemonic: A lunchbox sits under the attic, with a pole and a hatch beside it. Together they make a big building.
館.readingMnemonic: The building is shaped like a tin can. Can sounds like かん.

秋.meaningMnemonic: A campfire crackles beside the last wheat stalk in the field. The harvest is in, the leaves are falling, and it is autumn.
秋.readingMnemonic: You shuffle through the autumn leaves. Shuffle sounds like しゅう.

夏.meaningMnemonic: A plank over your self portrait, an eyeball staring, and dragging feet in the heat. It is summer.
夏.readingMnemonic: You take a road trip in the car every summer. Car sounds like か.

洋.meaningMnemonic: A ram with antlers, droplets everywhere, and a monarch swimming beside it. They are crossing the ocean.
洋.readingMnemonic: You play with a yoyo by the ocean. Yoyo sounds like よう.

旅.meaningMnemonic: A beggar reads the signpost at the edge of town. With a swoosh of his coat, he sets off on a long trip.
旅.readingMnemonic: A rioter ruins your trip. Rioter sounds like りょ.

夕.meaningMnemonic: The sun slips down, and the sky turns orange with dusk. That quiet time at the end of the day is evening.
夕.readingMnemonic: A sequin catches the evening light. Sequin sounds like せき.

終.meaningMnemonic: A spool lets out its tiny thread, and you follow it with dragging feet through a splash of mud. At last the thread runs out, and you reach the end.
終.readingMnemonic: You shuffle to the end of the line. Shuffle sounds like しゅう.

料.meaningMnemonic: You use the measuring scoop to dish out sparkler powder. Every scoop costs money, so you have to pay a fee.
料.readingMnemonic: You pay a fee to rent a leotard. Leotard sounds like りょう.

建.meaningMnemonic: With a quill you sketch plans for a huge slide. Then you gather wood and nails and start to build.
建.readingMnemonic: You build a kennel in the yard. Kennel sounds like けん.

空.meaningMnemonic: Under the attic, a burrow on stilts holds only a girder. Otherwise it is empty, open to the sky.
空.readingMnemonic: The empty sky feels cool. Cool sounds like くう.

切.meaningMnemonic: You try to slice the meat with a ladle, but it does not work. You swap the ladle for a cleaver, and now you can cut.
切.readingMnemonic: The setter dog cuts across the field. Setter sounds like せつ.

研.meaningMnemonic: By the hatch, on the bunk beds, you work on a pebble with pliers, a pole, a plank, and a fishhook, swoosh after swoosh. That is how you polish it.
研.readingMnemonic: You polish the kennel until it shines. Kennel sounds like けん.

足.meaningMnemonic: A hatch sits on top of the sneaker, and the sneaker halts at the stop sign. Your leg is inside.
足.readingMnemonic: You pull a sock over your leg. Sock sounds like そく.

究.meaningMnemonic: In the attic, you rest an elbow on the burrow, which stands on stilts. You are deep in research.
究.readingMnemonic: Every research project needs a cue. Cue sounds like きゅう.

楽.meaningMnemonic: A milk carton on timber, with icicles on each side, rings like a little xylophone. It is music.
楽.readingMnemonic: People stop to gawk at the music. Gawk sounds like がく.

起.meaningMnemonic: The sprinter kicks up soil and springs up like a coil. Time to rouse yourself.
起.readingMnemonic: You turn the key to rouse the engine. Key sounds like き.

病.meaningMnemonic: A walker lies under a goalpost on the sickbed, with a plank for a pillow. They are ill.
病.readingMnemonic: You fall ill in the bayou. Bayou sounds like びょう.

銀.meaningMnemonic: The ingot gives off a bright glare. It is silver.
銀.readingMnemonic: Ginkgo leaves shine like silver. Ginkgo sounds like ぎん.

験.meaningMnemonic: A walker with an umbrella checks the stallion through a hatch, then checks the embers. Every step needs verification.
験.readingMnemonic: The vet does a verification at the kennel. Kennel sounds like けん.

英.meaningMnemonic: Sprouts grow over a blanket and a starfish, swoosh go the rain clouds. It must be England.
英.readingMnemonic: An ace player comes from England. Ace sounds like えい.

医.meaningMnemonic: A dart lies on a tray beside a beggar. The doctor pulls it out.
医.readingMnemonic: The doctor is holding an eel. Eel sounds like い.

答.meaningMnemonic: In the bamboo grove, a beggar under an umbrella sits on a plank by a hatch. They know the solution.
答.readingMnemonic: The solution was under your toe all along. Toe sounds like とう.

帰.meaningMnemonic: You put down the rake and the sickle and fold the napkin and the blanket. It is time for the homecoming.
帰.readingMnemonic: You find your key at the homecoming. Key sounds like き.

歌.meaningMnemonic: A sneeze through the hatch sets a plank and a fishhook rattling. It turns into a song.
歌.readingMnemonic: You sing a song in the car. Car sounds like か.

買.meaningMnemonic: You drop a clam in your fishing net and keep an eyeball on the seller with the mustache. You decide to buy it.
買.readingMnemonic: You buy it and wave bye. Bye sounds like ばい.

図.meaningMnemonic: Inside a corral, you use a measuring scoop to mark every spot in the dirt. When you are done, you have drawn a map.
図.readingMnemonic: You need a map of the zoo. Zoo sounds like ず.

室.meaningMnemonic: Under the attic, the arrowhead lands in the soil at the finish line. This is your room.
室.readingMnemonic: Your comedy shtick fills the room. Shtick sounds like しつ.

風.meaningMnemonic: A gale knocks a beetle off the stool with a swoosh. That is the wind.
風.readingMnemonic: Only a fool fights the wind. Fool sounds like ふう.

紙.meaningMnemonic: The clan winds a tiny thread off the spool and mixes it with a splash of water. They press the mush flat and dry it into paper.
紙.readingMnemonic: You wrap the sheep in paper. Sheep sounds like し.

黒.meaningMnemonic: Embers burn the farmstead, and soot covers everything. It is all black.
黒.readingMnemonic: The cook burns the toast black. Cook sounds like こく.

花.meaningMnemonic: Your sidekick waters the sprouts with a ladle every morning. One day a bud opens into a flower.
花.readingMnemonic: A flower is stuck to the car. Car sounds like か.

赤.meaningMnemonic: The soil feels shy and starts to blush. The blush spreads across the ground until it is bright red.
赤.readingMnemonic: A red sequin glints on your sleeve. Sequin sounds like せき.

青.meaningMnemonic: A thumbtack, bunk beds, soil, and a crescent moon all lie out under a clear sky. The sky above them is a deep, clean blue.
青.readingMnemonic: Say the word blue. Say sounds like せい.

屋.meaningMnemonic: The arrowhead lands in the soil at the finish line, under an awning. It needs a proper roof.
屋.readingMnemonic: An oak grows right through the roof. Oak sounds like おく.

色.meaningMnemonic: Under a hood, you swirl a brush on your palette. The paints spin into a whirlpool of every color.
色.readingMnemonic: So much color comes as a shock. Shock sounds like しょく.

走.meaningMnemonic: A sprinter crouches at the line, then takes off. Soil flies up behind as the sprinter starts to run.
走.readingMnemonic: You run with soap in your eyes. Soap sounds like そう.

習.meaningMnemonic: A bird flaps its wings over a milk carton dripping icicles. It is starting to learn to fly.
習.readingMnemonic: You learn to shuffle cards. Shuffle sounds like しゅう.

駅.meaningMnemonic: A stallion waits under an awning, embers glowing, until a speck of a train appears. It is the station.
駅.readingMnemonic: You buy an eclair at the station. Eclair sounds like えき.

服.meaningMnemonic: Under the crescent moon, a kneeler holds up crossed fingers. She is wishing for new clothing.
服.readingMnemonic: You hang your clothing on a hook. Hook sounds like ふく.

借.meaningMnemonic: Your sidekick knocks on your door with an empty bag. First the pliers, then the bunk beds, and finally even the sun: your sidekick always wants to borrow something.
借.readingMnemonic: You borrow a shack for the summer. Shack sounds like しゃく.

曜.meaningMnemonic: A pigeon sits on a rake out in the sun, pecking at seeds. It shows up every single workday, so you use it to tell which weekday it is.
曜.readingMnemonic: On weekdays you play with a yoyo. Yoyo sounds like よう.

飲.meaningMnemonic: You open your lunchbox, and the dust makes you sneeze. Your throat is dry now, so you reach for something to drink.
飲.readingMnemonic: You stop for a drink at the inn. Inn sounds like いん.

貸.meaningMnemonic: Your sidekick drives a stake by the clam stall, one eyeball on the seller with the mustache. They agree to lend the seller a clam.
貸.readingMnemonic: You lend a friend your tie. Tie sounds like たい.

堂.meaningMnemonic: Steam rises over a hatch, with a blanket on the soil below. It is a public chamber where everyone gathers.
堂.readingMnemonic: A doe wanders into the hall. Doe sounds like どう.

冬.meaningMnemonic: Dragging feet through the snow, you drop your baton, and a speck of ice hits your nose. It is winter.
冬.readingMnemonic: Winter bites your toe. Toe sounds like とう.

昼.meaningMnemonic: Under the awning, the sun stands right over a plank, with not a speck of shade. It is daytime.
昼.readingMnemonic: You chew your lunch at noon. Chew sounds like ちゅう.

茶.meaningMnemonic: Sprouts grow under an umbrella on a stack of timber. You pick the leaves and brew tea.
茶.readingMnemonic: There is lots of chatter over tea. Chatter sounds like ちゃ.

弟.meaningMnemonic: A little boy puts on toy antlers and pretends to be an archer. He swings a pole around with a swoosh, the way only a younger brother would.
弟.readingMnemonic: Your younger brother wraps everything in tape. Tape sounds like てい.

牛.meaningMnemonic: An ox stands in the field, chewing slowly. On the farm, that big gentle animal is a cow.
牛.readingMnemonic: The cow steps in something gooey. Gooey sounds like ぎゅう.

兄.meaningMnemonic: Someone tall walks by on stilts, with a head as wide as a hatch. You have to look up at him, because he is your elder brother.
兄.readingMnemonic: Your elder brother eats all the cake. Cake sounds like けい.

妹.meaningMnemonic: The dancer is your younger sister. She pins a thumbtack to a pole and draws a mustache on the timber of the bunk beds.
妹.readingMnemonic: Your younger sister keeps pet mice. Mice sounds like まい.

姉.meaningMnemonic: The dancer pins up a napkin with a thumbtack. That dancer is your elder sister.
姉.readingMnemonic: Your elder sister herds sheep. Sheep sounds like し.

漢.meaningMnemonic: Droplets fall on sprouts by a hatch, and a starfish naps on a plank and bunk beds by the river. It is a scene from old China, where Sino- words come from.
漢.readingMnemonic: Chinese tea comes in a can. Can sounds like かん.

政.meaningMnemonic: A beggar waves a baton at a stop sign nailed to a plank, shouting slogans. That is politics.
政.readingMnemonic: Politicians say a lot. Say sounds like せい.

民.meaningMnemonic: Under the awning, a clan pours out of a hatch. They are the people.
民.readingMnemonic: The people love mint. Mint sounds like みん.

連.meaningMnemonic: You hitch your wagon to the conveyor belt. Wherever the belt goes, the wagon comes too, and you take it along.
連.readingMnemonic: You take a friend along to pay the rent. Rent sounds like れん.

対.meaningMnemonic: A sheet of calligraphy hangs on one wall, and an inch ruler hangs on the wall across. The two face each other, sitting vis-a-vis.
対.readingMnemonic: Opposite you sits someone in a tie. Tie sounds like たい.

合.meaningMnemonic: The umbrella closes over a plank on the hatch. They fit together perfectly.
合.readingMnemonic: The ball fits right in the goal. Goal sounds like ごう.

市.meaningMnemonic: A napkin is pinned to a post with a thumbtack. It is the sign for a food stall, and there are rows of them at the market.
